_readme:
Codex typed items and raw model items use separate vocabulary tables. Both the Go provider and TypeScript plugin read these tables. Native exec has raw request and output items without a typed command mirror. Exact thread, turn, and call identity pairs those rows.

Codex streams command output through outputDelta events and fills aggregatedOutput on the completed typed item. LeapMux stores retained deltas beside an incomplete item. The supplement keys belong to LeapMux. Native item keys belong to OpenAI. The control tool names and the async question input keys belong to LeapMux.

The controlTools table lists the tool names of the control requests that LeapMux publishes for Codex itself: the plan-mode prompt and an async question. The asyncQuestionInput table holds the keys of one async question input. Codex asks the question without waiting. The browser shows it as a non-blocking control request, and the worker builds the reply envelope from the question_item_id identity.

The options and optionDefaults tables keep shared option IDs and launch values consistent. The worker builds its option groups from them. The browser uses the same values for agent configuration. The permission_profile axis holds a Codex permission profile ID, such as :workspace. It replaced the legacy sandbox_policy and network_access axes, because upstream Codex now selects permissions by profile.

The autoReviewStatus and autoReviewActions tables hold the words of an item/autoApprovalReview/completed notification. The browser reads them to draw an auto-review row. The worker reads them to convert a denied review into the core event that thread/approveGuardianDeniedAction accepts.

The executables table lists the names that the worker probes on the search path, in preference order. The worker starts the first name that the shell finds. The second name is the full Rust host triple that `cargo install` produces on Windows when the shorter codex shim is absent. The E2E suite reads the same list, so it skips the Codex specs only when the worker cannot find any of the names.

The execOutput table holds native output values that storage filtering and browser extraction both read.

A code-mode cell that yields keeps running, and the model reads the rest of its output through `wait` calls. Each yield returns only the output since the yield before it. The worker joins a waited cell into one card: the exec request row, and the exec output row with each later wait output beside it in a CodexExecSupplement. The callId identifies the exec output that the supplement belongs to. The execOutput RunningHeaderPrefix opens the header of a yield, and both sides read it.

ThreadNameUpdated.why: The protocol catalog includes this method, but Codex sends it only after thread/name/set, which LeapMux never sends. Neither side has a special reader.

ThreadCompacted.why: The protocol catalog includes this deprecated method, but Codex 0.163 does not emit it. Native contextCompaction item completions carry the boundary.

InProgress.why: The worker persists only the completed review, whose status is never in progress, so the browser never draws one. The worker still reads the word to convert every status into its core spelling.

QuestionItemID.why: The worker builds the reply from this identity. The browser shows only the title and the options.

CodexToolSupplement.doc: CodexToolSupplement stores the output that LeapMux joined for an incomplete typed tool call. The item identity keeps the supplement on its original row.

CodexExecSupplement.doc: CodexExecSupplement stores the wait outputs of a code-mode cell that yielded, in order. The call identity keeps the supplement on the exec output row that it continues.

CodexRawExecutionItem.doc: CodexRawExecutionItem reads native exec identity and payload fields. A nullable input distinguishes an empty script from missing source.

CodexRawExecutionParams.doc: CodexRawExecutionParams identifies the native thread and turn of one raw response item. The item remains raw until its type is known.

CodexAsyncQuestionInput.doc: CodexAsyncQuestionInput is the input of one LeapMux-owned async question request. The question identity lets the worker build Codex's reply envelope.
